spatial_claims.claim: G falls between F and H on the line (since CD < AB implies FG < FH), and GH = FH - FG
Rectangle (FH+FG) x GH = FH^2 - FG^2 by the difference of squares identity (2.1)

configuration_map: All construction occurs on a single line. EF is a rational straight line. FH is a segment (breadth of medial area AB applied to EF). FG is a segment (breadth of medial area CD applied to EF), with G between F and H since CD < AB. GH = FH - FG is the remaining segment. No triangles, circles, angles, or genuinely spatial constructions exist. The entire proof reasons about commensurability relations among these collinear segments and the areas they determine.
skip_reason: The proof is purely algebraic, dealing with commensurability and incommensurability of lengths and areas (Book 10 irrational theory). The only spatial content is the trivial betweenness of G between F and H on a line. There are no angle decompositions, no triangle interior/exterior claims, no circle configurations, and no ray orderings — nothing that could produce a geometric configuration contradiction.
